html:
The Barngarla, once spelled Parnkalla or Pangkala, are an Aboriginal Australian people of South Australia and the traditional owners of much of Eyre Peninsula, including the areas of today's Port Augusta, Whyalla and Port Lincoln.

Their language belongs to the Yura group. In 1844 the Lutheran missionary Clamor Schürmann published a vocabulary of it, and this record now underpins an effort to revive the language led with the linguist Ghil'ad Zuckermann at the University of Adelaide.

Neighbours included the Nukunu across the gulf, the Nauo to the southwest and the Kokatha to the north. After 1839 sheep runs spread over the peninsula. In 2015 the Federal Court recognised Barngarla native title over a large part of it.
sum: The Barngarla, once spelled Parnkalla or Pangkala, are an Aboriginal Australian people of South Australia and the traditional owners of much of Eyre Peninsula, including the areas of today's Port Augusta, Whyalla and Port Lincoln.
